  • export, export_all: Publication export to PDF/PNG/SVG/CSV.

docs.title: 3. Scientific Spectroscopy & Hyperspectral Operations
docs.text:
• spectrum_1d: 1D continuous spectral curve showing characteristic emission/absorption peaks.
  • map_2d: 2D spatial hyperspectral raster / false-color intensity map.
  • wafer_map: Circular semiconductor wafer map with notch orientation and spatial coordinate dies.
  • baseline: Sub-spectral baseline subtraction (polynomial, rubberband, ALS).
  • peak: Deconvoluted individual peak curve (Gaussian, Lorentzian, Voigt, Pseudo-Voigt).
  • bestfit: Vectorized Batch Fit (VBF) composite model curve overlaid on raw data.
  • norm: Intensity normalization (\([0, 1]\), standard normal variate, area normalization).
  • stats: Statistical distribution summary curve, mean \(\pm\) standard deviation envelope.
  • calc: Spectral math operations (derivative, integration, ratio calculation).

docs.title: 4. Graphing & Publication Plotting
docs.text:
• graph_line: Multi-series continuous line plot.
  • graph_scatter: Discrete experimental point scatter plot.
  • graph_bar: Categorical bar plot.
  • graph_box: Statistical box-and-whisker distribution.
  • graph_histogram: Binned frequency histogram.
  • graph_trendline: Linear or polynomial regression fit curve with confidence bounds.
  • styling / palette_color: Colormap selector and plot theme editor.
  • legend: Toggle floating graph legend.
  • zoom: Box zoom region tool.
  • pan: 2D drag navigation tool.
  • rescale: Reset axes view to data bounding box.

docs.title: 5. Embedded AI Assistant & Status
docs.text:
• sparkles: AI chat assistant invocation / intelligent peak suggestion.
  • brain: Model reasoning / semantic memory indexer.
  • send: Submit AI chat prompt.
  • stop: Abort ongoing VBF fitting iteration or AI response stream.
  • mic: Voice input transcription.
  • paperclip: Attach spectrum or dataset to AI context.
  • activity: Background optimizer activity heartbeat.

docs.title: 7. Migration & Compatibility Plan
docs.text:
1. tokens.py & ThemeTokens:
  2. Update ThemeTokens dataclass to match PLUME's 36-token specification.
  3. Replace old token palettes with PLUME DARK_TOKENS and LIGHT_TOKENS.
  4. Update ThemeManager to retire "modern_warm" and provide seamless migration to "light".
  5. QSS Stylesheet Overhaul (qss_template.py):
  6. Rebuild the global stylesheet referencing PLUME's compact geometry (18-22px inputs, 6px/8px radii, 5px visible splitters).
  7. Ensure all rgba(...) declarations use integer alpha values (0..255).
  8. Vector SVG Infrastructure (icons_svg.py & icons.py):
  9. Introduce icons_svg.py hosting _SvgIconEngine, _SVG_TEMPLATES, svg_icon(), and svg_pixmap().
  10. Wrap legacy calls (get_tinted_icon(path, color)) in spectroview/viewmodel/common/ui_utils.py (re-exported in viewmodel/utils.py) and workspace view classes so existing code works transparently without breakage.
  11. Native Windows DWM Synchronization (winapi/ or ThemeManager):
  12. Wire native caption/border theming for top-level windows on Windows 11.

docs.title: Developer Guide: Vectorized Batch Fit Engine (VBF)
docs.text: This document provides a deep dive into the inner workings, architecture, and performance characteristics of the Vectorized Batch Fit Engine (VBF) located in spectroview/fit_engine/.

docs.title: 1. Why the VBF Engine Is Much Faster
docs.text:
The legacy fit engines operate on a per-spectrum basis. For a hyperspectral map containing thousands of spectra, this approach introduces significant overhead:

  • Python Function Call Overhead: Calling the objective function and Jacobian estimator thousands of times per iteration.
  • Finite-Difference Jacobians: Approximating the Jacobian numerically requires 2 * K (where K is the number of parameters) additional function evaluations per iteration, per spectrum.
  • Sequential Execution: Even with multiprocessing, the overhead of serialization and inter-process communication creates bottlenecks.

The Vectorized Batch Fit Engine (VBF Engine) achieves massive speedups through the following core principles:

  1. All-at-Once Optimization: It optimizes all \(N\) spectra simultaneously. The parameter matrices, data arrays, and residuals are manipulated as large 2D or 3D tensors.
  2. Vectorized Operations (BLAS/LAPACK): By framing the problem as tensors, the heavy lifting is offloaded to highly optimized C/Fortran libraries.
    • Matrix multiplications and transpositions for the normal equations (\(J^T J\) and \(J^T r\)) are performed using np.matmul, which dispatches to a batched BLAS gemm call. (An earlier version used np.einsum for this; einsum does not dispatch to BLAS for this contraction pattern and was measured 13–20× slower — see §2.)
    • The linear systems for all spectra are solved via batched np.linalg.solve directly across (Na, K, K) (np.linalg.solve(A, b[..., None])[..., 0]), dispatching all independent solves in a single LAPACK batch call instead of a Python loop, with per-matrix Cholesky/np.linalg.solve/0.0 strictly as a singular-matrix LinAlgError fallback. See _batched_solve() in §2.
  3. Analytical Jacobians: Instead of estimating derivatives numerically, the engine uses exact analytical formulas for every registered peak shape (Gaussian, Lorentzian, PseudoVoigt, GaussianAsym, LorentzianAsym, Fano, DecaySingleExp, DecayBiExp). This eliminates the \(2K\) extra evaluations entirely.
  4. No Spatial Propagation: Unlike older map-fitting approaches that used spiral traversal to propagate guesses from neighbor to neighbor (forcing sequential execution), the VBF Engine initializes all pixels independently using amplitude scaling, allowing purely parallel tensor math.
  5. Variable Length Support: When spectra don't share a common x-axis, x is passed as an (N, M) matrix instead of (M,), and every batched model/Jacobian function branches on x.ndim to broadcast per-row instead of per-column.
  6. Expression Support: Supports complex mathematical relationships between parameters across the batch by evaluating mathematical constraints symbolically before mapping to free parameters.

docs.title: 2. Performance Optimizations
docs.text:
The items below are specific to the numerical core in fit_engine/. Preprocessing-level optimizations (range cropping, baseline evaluation over the whole map tensor) live in SpectraStore.batch_preprocess() and are documented in spectra_store.md.

  1. Batched normal-equation assembly via np.matmul instead of np.einsum (13–20× faster for \(J^TJ\), 3–4× for \(J^Tr\), measured across realistic N/M/K sizes): np.einsum('nmk,nml->nkl', J, J) does not dispatch to BLAS for this contraction pattern and falls back to a generic reduction loop. The mathematically identical J.transpose(0, 2, 1) @ J dispatches to a batched BLAS gemm call.
  2. Skip redundant Jacobian/normal-equation recomputation for rejected steps: a rejected LM trial leaves a spectrum's parameters unchanged, so its Jacobian — and therefore \(J^TJ\)/\(J^Tr\) — is still exactly valid; only the damping term needs to change before retrying. optimizer.py caches \(J^TJ\)/\(J^Tr\) per spectrum (JTJ_cache, JTr_cache) and only recomputes them for spectra whose last step was accepted (tracked via a dirty boolean array), instead of for every active spectrum on every iteration. This is exact, not an approximation — verified to add zero additional numerical drift versus eager recomputation. On a slow-converging map (many spectra retrying at the same point under increasing damping), roughly 30% of active-spectrum iterations are rejected steps, so this directly eliminates ~30% of the two most expensive per-iteration operations.
  3. Guarded np.nan_to_num: np.nan_to_num runs three separate full-array passes (isnan/isposinf/isneginf) plus fancy-index assignment, even when nothing is actually wrong — true on the overwhelming majority of iterations. optimizer._finite_or_clean() checks np.isfinite(arr).all() first (a single fused pass) and only pays for the cleanup when something needs fixing — ~10× faster on the common, clean path.
  4. Zero-Temporary In-Place Model & Jacobian Kernels: every function in models.py computes each repeated quantity (1/w², 1/w³, dx², …) once and reuses it, replacing repeated (N,M)-sized divisions with a single (N,1) reciprocal plus a broadcasted multiply (inv_wl = 1.0 / wl, inv_wr = 1.0 / wr), and writing directly into pre-allocated out= buffers from the first arithmetic operation (np.subtract(..., out=out)). All 8 analytical Jacobian functions (batched_*_jac) write partial derivatives directly into J[:, :, k] slice views in place and exploit the algebraic identity \(\frac{\partial f}{\partial w} = \frac{x - x_0}{w} \frac{\partial f}{\partial x_0}\) (J[:, :, 1] = dx * J[:, :, 2] * inv_w), eliminating 3–6 temporary (N, M) heap allocations per peak per iteration. Scalar reference models in scalar_models.py use identical 1e-15 width and 1e-30 lifetime clamping to guarantee machine-precision parity (\(\le 10^{-13}\)) with BATCHED_MODELS.
  5. Shared noise-floor statistics, 2D memoization & O(N) peak-index lookup: apply_noise_threshold() runs once before the fit (to seed a clean initial guess) and once after (to clean up any peaks that drifted into a noisy region — see §5.2 and §10). Both calls reuse statistics cached by VBFevaluator.compute_noise_stats(), while noise.py caches 1-entry mutation-safe 2D fingerprints (_array_2d_fingerprint) so back-to-back calls to compute_fit_weights(Y, fit_params) and compute_noise_stats(Y, coef_noise) do not recompute mad_noise(Y) and moving_average_5(Y) twice on the same matrix. Peak-to-grid index lookup uses O(1) uniform arithmetic, O(N log M) np.searchsorted, or chunk-256 fallback instead of allocating an (N, M) distance matrix.
  6. Batched Linear Solver (_batched_solve()): dispatches all active (Na, K, K) normal-equation systems through a single NumPy batched np.linalg.solve(A, b[..., None])[..., 0] call regardless of batch size or parameter count, retaining per-matrix SciPy cho_solve / np.linalg.solve / 0.0 strictly as a singular-matrix LinAlgError fallback.
  7. Post-Clip Mean-Based Convergence Criteria: the convergence check measures mean(|dp_actual| / |p|) < xtol using actual post-clip displacement (p_trial_active - p_improved_old) rather than unconstrained dp or max(), preventing both slowly drifting wings and bound-pinned parameters from stalling spectra until max_iter.
  8. Vectorized Write-Back: build_results_batch() evaluates all best-fit curves and computes R² simultaneously across all spectra using a single reusable (N, M) residual buffer and skipping redundant multiplications when weights is uniform ones — no per-spectrum Python loop.
  9. Zero-Weight Early Exit & Uniform-Weights Fast Path: spectra identified as pure noise (all weights zero) are marked converged instantly, and weights of None or uniform 1.0 bypass per-iteration (N, M) weighted residual/Jacobian multiplications.
  10. Transposed (K, N, M) Jacobian Layout & Zero-Copy Full-Batch Fast Paths: batched_levenberg_marquardt() allocates J_buf_base with physical layout (K, N, M) and exposes J_r_buf = J_buf_base[:, :n_recompute, :].transpose(1, 2, 0) of logical shape (Nr, M, K). This guarantees that every parameter slice J[:, :, k] is a 100% C-contiguous (Nr, M) array during Jacobian evaluation AND that the contraction axis M has stride 8 bytes during JT_r @ J_r and JT_r @ scaled_r_r[:, :, None] BLAS dgemm calls. On early iterations where all spectra are active (n_active == N, n_recompute == N), the optimizer uses zero-copy views and writes normal equations directly into JTJ_cache and JTr_cache via np.matmul(..., out=...) without fancy-index gathers.
  11. Forward-Mode Dual-Number (_DualVar) Analytical Chain Rule for Expressions: VBFevaluator topologically sorts and bytecode-compiles parameter expressions once in from_fit_model(), and computes exact analytical chain-rule derivatives J_expr in a single pass using vectorized forward-mode automatic differentiation (_DualVar) coupled with batched BLAS matrix multiplication (J_full @ J_expr), replacing \(K_{\text{free}}\)-pass finite differences and np.einsum (~3× faster on expression-constrained models).
  12. Adaptive L3-Cache Batch Chunking: when fitting very large hyperspectral maps (\(N \cdot M \cdot K > 2{,}097{,}152\) or \(N \ge 2{,}048\) with \(N \cdot M \cdot K > 1{,}048{,}576\)), batched_levenberg_marquardt() automatically partitions the batch into L3-cache-friendly sub-batches (chunk_n targeting ~4 MB working footprint), reducing peak memory usage by up to 79% and accelerating large-map fits by avoiding DRAM bandwidth saturation.
  13. Pure-NumPy Linear Baseline Interpolation: eval_baseline() and eval_baseline_batch() evaluate piecewise linear baselines (with domain-edge linear extrapolation) via _interp_linear_extrap() in pure NumPy, eliminating cold scipy.interpolate import overhead.

docs.title: 3. Code Logic and Core Implementation Principles
docs.text: The engine implements a Batched Levenberg-Marquardt algorithm.

docs.title: 3.1. The Mathematics of Batched LM
docs.text:
For \(N\) spectra, each with \(M\) wavelength points and \(K\) free parameters:

  1. Evaluate Model: \(\mathbf{Y}_{pred} = f(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{p})\), returning an \((N, M)\) tensor.
  2. Calculate Residuals: \(\mathbf{r} = \mathbf{W} \circ (\mathbf{Y}_{pred} - \mathbf{Y}_{data})\), returning an \((N, M)\) tensor.
  3. Calculate Jacobian: \(\mathbf{J} = \frac{\partial f}{\partial \mathbf{p}}\), returning an \((N, M, K)\) tensor.
  4. Normal Equations: Assemble \(J^T J\) (size \(N \times K \times K\)) and \(J^T r\) (size \(N \times K\)) via np.matmul (§2).
  5. Damping (Marquardt step): Add a damping factor \(\lambda_i\) to the diagonal of \(J^T J\) for each spectrum \(i\).
  6. Solve: Solve \((J^T J + \lambda \text{diag}(J^T J)) \delta \mathbf{p} = -J^T r\) for all \(N\) spectra simultaneously.
  7. Evaluate Step: Update \(\mathbf{p} \leftarrow \mathbf{p} + \delta \mathbf{p}\) (with projection to bounds) and evaluate the new cost. Adjust \(\lambda\) per spectrum based on success/failure.

docs.title: 3.2. Independent Convergence
docs.text: Even though the math is batched, each spectrum converges independently. The optimizer uses a boolean mask (active = ~converged) to skip Jacobian calculations and linear solves for spectra that have already reached the tolerance limits, progressively speeding up the later iterations. A second boolean mask (dirty, see §2) further skips the Jacobian/normal-equation computation — but not the trial-step evaluation — for active spectra whose parameters didn't change on the previous iteration (a rejected step), since only the damping factor differs on the retry.

docs.title: 3.3. Robust Loss Functions (IRLS-Style Scaling)
docs.text:
To handle outliers such as cosmic ray spikes and sharp detector artifacts without requiring manual data masking, the optimizer supports robust M-estimators via Iteratively Reweighted Least Squares (IRLS):

  • linear (default): Standard least-squares objective \(\rho(z) = z\), \(\rho'(z) = 1\). The code path is bit-identical to the original unweighted LM.
  • soft_l1: Smooth \(L_1\) approximation \(\rho(z) = 2(\sqrt{1 + z} - 1)\), with derivative scaling factor \(\sqrt{\rho'(z)} = (1 + z)^{-1/4}\) where \(z = (r / f\_scale)^2\). Transitions smoothly from quadratic behavior near zero to linear penalty for large residuals.
  • huber: Huber loss \(\rho(z) = z\) if \(z \le 1\) else \(2\sqrt{z} - 1\), with derivative scaling factor \(\sqrt{\rho'(z)} = 1\) if \(z \le 1\) else \(z^{-1/4}\).

Mathematical Formulation: Residuals and Jacobian rows are scaled by \(w_{\text{robust}} = \sqrt{\rho'((r / f\_scale)^2)}\). The normal equations solved at each iteration are: $\((J^T W J + \lambda \text{diag}(J^T W J)) \delta \mathbf{p} = -J^T W \mathbf{r}\)$ where \(W = \text{diag}(w_{\text{hard}}^2 \cdot w_{\text{robust}}^2)\).

Weighting Composition Order:

  1. Hard exclusions (fit_negative and coef_noise noise floor) are evaluated first in weights.py to assign zero weight (\(w_{\text{hard}} = 0\)) to excluded points.
  2. Robust weighting (\(w_{\text{robust}}\)) is applied second inside optimizer.py on the active points, smoothly down-weighting large outlier residuals. Zero-weighted points remain zero.

docs.title: 4. Folder and Class Structure
docs.text:
graph TD
    TFT["VBFthread"] -->|"instantiates"| TE["VBFengine"]
    TE -->|"builds"| EV["VBFevaluator"]
    TE -->|"calls"| OPT["batched_LM()"]
    EV -->|"routes to"| MOD["models.py"]
    OPT -->|"evaluate / jacobian"| EV
Module Class / Function Responsibility vbf_thread.py VBFthread QThread wrapper. Groups tasks into single-map, mega-batch (grouped_2d_maps), or length-grouped (map_names) modes; builds the weights matrix; calls VBFengine.fit_spectra(); writes results back into SpectraStore. Emits progress_changed and timings_ready signals. Sets an 8 MB stack on macOS to prevent LAPACK segfaults. vbf_engine.py VBFengine Public API orchestrator for a single fit call. Builds the evaluator, builds p0 + applies the noise threshold, runs the optimizer, re-applies the noise threshold, and builds the result arrays. Records step-level timings in self.timings. evaluator.py VBFevaluator Bridge between the dictionary-based fit_model and the flat tensor API. Parses peak definitions, manages free/fixed parameter indexing, evaluates expressions, routes to the correct batched model functions, and builds the returned result arrays (parameters, R², best fits, per-peak curves) — no intermediate FitResult objects. optimizer.py batched_levenberg_marquardt() Pure numerical optimizer. Solves N independent least-squares problems simultaneously using batched np.matmul for the normal equations, with JᵀJ/Jᵀr caching to skip recomputation for rejected trial steps (§2). Uses batched np.linalg.solve with per-matrix singular fallback, reuses eval_buf/J_buf via out=, skips uniform weights, and checks post-clip dp convergence. GUI-agnostic. models.py batched_*() functions Vectorized peak shape functions and their analytical Jacobians. Contains the BATCHED_MODELS registry and the numerical_jacobian() fallback for models without one. scalar_models.py scalar peak functions Single-spectrum reference implementations, and the PEAK_MODEL_REGISTRY they're registered under. Used by eval_peak_initial() (UI preview curves) and as the scalar fallback wrapped by _make_batched_scalar() in evaluator.py when a model exists in PEAK_MODEL_REGISTRY but has no batched implementation in BATCHED_MODELS — currently every registered model has both, so this fallback path is a safety net for future additions rather than something exercised today.

docs.title: 5. Processing Pipeline / Execution Flow
docs.text:
The pipeline has two levels: VBFthread orchestrates tasks (which spectra go together, how weights are built, where results are written), and VBFengine.fit_spectra() is the pure numerical core called once per task.

sequenceDiagram
    participant VM as ViewModel
    participant TFT as VBFthread
    participant TE as VBFengine
    participant EV as VBFevaluator
    participant OPT as optimizer

    VM->>TFT: start()
    TFT->>TFT: _prepare_weights() — negative-value & noise masking
    TFT->>TE: fit_spectra(x, Y, fit_model, weights, fit_params)
    TE->>EV: from_fit_model()
    TE->>EV: build_p0_matrix() + apply_noise_threshold() (pre-fit)
    TE->>OPT: batched_levenberg_marquardt()
    TE->>EV: apply_noise_threshold() (post-fit cleanup)
    TE->>EV: build_results_batch()
    TE-->>TFT: p_full, success, r², best_fits, Y_peaks
    TFT->>TFT: _write_results() → store.set_fit_results(), md.Y_bestfit / md.Y_peaks
    TFT-->>VM: progress_changed / timings_ready / finished

docs.title: 5.1. VBFthread.run() — Task Orchestration
docs.text:
For each task, VBFthread picks one of three branches inside a single loop over self.tasks (there is no separate _run_batched()/_run_single() method):

Task key present When used What happens grouped_2d_maps "Apply model to all maps" with a shared model np.vstacks every map's Y into one matrix, fits it as a single mega-batch, then scatters the results back into each MapData by row range. map_names Spectra workspace batch-fitting many single spectra, each with its own model Groups spectra by x-axis length (spectra must share length to stack into one matrix) and fits each length-group as one batch. map_name + indices Fitting one map (the common case) Extracts Y[indices], builds weights, calls fit_spectra() once.

Before calling into the engine, VBFthread._prepare_weights() builds the weights matrix from fit_negative and coef_noise (see §9 and §10 — the noise-based masking here uses the same formula as VBFevaluator.compute_noise_stats()).

docs.title: 5.2. VBFengine.fit_spectra() — The Numerical Core
docs.text:
1. Build the evaluator — VBFevaluator.from_fit_model(fit_model) parses peak_models into the flat parameter layout (§6). If every parameter is fixed (n_params_free == 0), the engine short-circuits and returns immediately.
  2. Build p0 — build_p0_matrix() tiles the model's initial values across all N spectra and rescales each peak's amplitude to the observed data at that peak's x0 (the ratio is clamped to [0.01, 100] so a bad guess can't explode). apply_noise_threshold() then zeroes amplitude/FWHM for peaks whose center sits in a below-noise-floor region, giving the optimizer a clean starting point.
  3. Run the optimizer — batched_levenberg_marquardt() (§3) iterates until every spectrum has converged, is marked "stuck" (§9.2), or max_ite is reached.
  4. Post-fit cleanup — apply_noise_threshold() runs again on the optimized parameters, in case any peak drifted into a noise region during the LM iterations.
  5. Build results — build_results_batch() evaluates the best-fit curves and per-peak curves once for the whole batch and computes R² vectorized across all N spectra. Returns plain arrays (p_full, success, rsquared, best_fits, Y_peaks, param_names) — not per-spectrum objects.

VBFthread._write_results() then writes those arrays into the SpectraStore (set_fit_results()) and onto the MapData object (Y_bestfit, Y_peaks).

docs.title: 6. The VBFevaluator in Detail
docs.text: The VBFevaluator is the most complex class in the engine. It serves as the bridge between the flexible, dictionary-based world of the GUI and the rigid, flat-tensor world of the optimizer.

docs.title: 6.2. Expression Support
docs.text:
Parameters can reference other parameters via mathematical expressions (e.g., m01_fwhm = m02_fwhm or m01_x0 + 10). The evaluator handles this in _to_full():

  1. Parameters with expressions are marked as fixed (not optimized directly).
  2. During from_fit_model(), expressions are topologically sorted by dependency and compiled into Python code objects (_compile_exprs()), avoiding repeated eval() string parsing and retry loops on every optimizer step.
  3. During _to_full(), compiled expressions are evaluated in a single topological pass using a restricted namespace containing all parameter names, np, and common math functions (sin, cos, tan, exp, log, log10, sqrt, abs, pi, e, minimum, maximum, clip).
  4. The Jacobian accounts for expressions via the analytical chain rule: _compute_j_expr() seeds free parameters as vectorized forward-mode dual numbers (_DualVar(value, d_free)) and executes the compiled expression chain once to obtain the exact analytical sensitivity tensor J_expr of shape (N, K_total, K_free), then computes the constrained Jacobian via batched BLAS matrix multiplication J_full @ J_expr.

docs.title: 6.3. Model Routing
docs.text:
The evaluator's evaluate() and jacobian() methods iterate over all registered peaks and write or sum their contributions cleanly into out when provided:

def evaluate(self, x, p_free, out=None):
    p_full = p_free if self._all_free_identity else self._to_full(p_free)  # (N, K_total)
    # Single-peak models write directly into `out`; multi-peak models reuse one scratch buffer
    ...

For the Jacobian, if a peak has an analytical Jacobian (has_jac=True), it is used directly. Otherwise, numerical_jacobian() is called as a fallback with central differences and relative perturbation scaling.

docs.title: 7. Batched Peak Models and Analytical Jacobians
7.1. Tensor Conventions
docs.text:
All batched functions follow the same signature:

def batched_shape(x, params, out=None):
    """
    x:      (M,) shared axis  OR  (N, M) per-spectrum axis
    params: (N, n_p) parameter matrix
    out:    optional preallocated (N, M) output buffer
    Returns: (N, M) predicted values
    """

def batched_shape_jac(x, params, out=None):
    """Returns: (N, M, n_p) Jacobian tensor (written into `out` when provided)"""

Internally, every function follows the same efficiency pattern (§2.4): compute each repeated quantity once (typically a reciprocal like 1/w²), reuse it via broadcasted multiplication instead of re-dividing, and write into pre-allocated Jacobian slices in place.

docs.title: 7.2. Registered Models (BATCHED_MODELS)
docs.text:
All peak models have vectorized batched implementations with analytical Jacobians, ensuring maximum performance for every model type:

Model Parameters Formula Gaussian ampli, fwhm, x0 a · exp(-4 ln(2) · (x-x0)2 / w2) Lorentzian ampli, fwhm, x0 a / [1 + 4(x-x0)2 / w2] PseudoVoigt ampli, fwhm, x0, alpha α · G + (1-α) · L GaussianAsym ampli, fwhm_l, fwhm_r, x0 Piecewise Gaussian with left/right FWHM LorentzianAsym ampli, fwhm_l, fwhm_r, x0 Piecewise Lorentzian with left/right FWHM Fano ampli, fwhm, x0, q a · (q + ε)2 / (1 + ε2), ε = 2(x-x0)/w DecaySingleExp A, tau, B A · e-x/τ + B DecayBiExp A1, tau1, A2, tau2, B A1 · e-x/τ1 + A2 · e-x/τ2 + B

docs.title: 7.3. Numerical Jacobian Fallback
docs.text:
For future custom models registered only in PEAK_MODEL_REGISTRY (without a batched implementation), numerical_jacobian() uses central differences with relative perturbation as a fallback:

h = max(|param| * eps, eps)          # Scale step to parameter magnitude
J[:,:,k] = (f(p+h) - f(p-h)) / 2h  # Central difference

This is ~2K times slower than analytical Jacobians per iteration but ensures correctness for any model shape.

docs.title: 8.1. Task Branches
docs.text:
graph TD
    TFT["VBFthread.run()"] --> Check{"task keys?"}
    Check -->|"grouped_2d_maps"| G["Mega-batch: vstack all maps, fit once, scatter back"]
    Check -->|"map_names"| B["Group spectra by x-axis length, fit each group"]
    Check -->|"map_name + indices"| S["Single map: fit once"]

All three branches live inside one loop over self.tasks in run() — see §5.1 for what triggers each one.

docs.title: 8.2. macOS Stack Size
docs.text:
The thread sets an 8 MB stack size on macOS (setStackSize(8 * 1024 * 1024)) because:

  • macOS defaults QThread stack to 512 KB.
  • np.linalg.solve dispatches to LAPACK, which allocates workspace arrays on the stack.
  • For large K (many parameters), the stack allocation can exceed 512 KB, causing segfaults.

docs.title: 8.3. Signals
docs.text: Signal Payload Purpose progress_changed Signal(int, int, int, float, int) → (current, total, percent, elapsed_seconds, current) Updates progress bar in the View. (The 5th argument duplicates the 1st.) timings_ready Signal(str) Formatted per-step timing breakdown for console/debug

docs.title: 9. Optimization Parameters and Adjustments
docs.text: The engine behavior can be tuned via the fit_params dictionary passed to fit_spectra().

docs.title: 9.1. Key Parameters
docs.text:
• max_ite (default: 200): The maximum number of Levenberg-Marquardt iterations. Increasing this might help extremely difficult spectra converge but will increase total execution time.
  • xtol (default: 1e-4): The relative tolerance for the parameter step size \(\delta p\). Convergence is reached when the mean relative post-clip change across all active parameters (\(\operatorname{mean}(|\Delta p_{\text{actual}}| / |p|)\)) is less than xtol. Measuring post-clip displacement ensures that spectra pinned at parameter bounds converge cleanly instead of stalling until max_ite, and the mean-based criterion prevents a single slowly oscillating parameter from delaying convergence for the entire spectrum.
  • ftol (default: 1e-4): The relative tolerance for the cost function (sum of squared residuals). If the relative change in the cost is less than ftol, the spectrum is considered converged.
  • fit_negative (default: False): Whether to include negative intensity values in the fit. When False, negative points receive zero weight (VBFthread._prepare_weights()).
  • coef_noise (default: 0.0): Noise coefficient multiplier. When > 0, activates noise-based weight masking (VBFthread._prepare_weights()) and peak suppression (VBFevaluator.apply_noise_threshold()). See Section 10 for a detailed explanation.
  • fit_outliers — legacy key, not read by the current engine. Older saved fit_model JSON files may still contain it, but nothing in fit_engine/ (or anywhere else in the codebase) checks it anymore; it's silently ignored. Safe to leave in old files.

docs.title: 9.2. Tuning for Performance vs. Accuracy
docs.text:
• Fast Mapping: For rapid previews, you can increase xtol and ftol to 1e-3 or 1e-2. The optimizer will exit much earlier, providing a rough fit in a fraction of the time.
  • Precision Fitting: For publication-quality results, decrease xtol and ftol to 1e-5 or 1e-6.
  • Handling "Stuck" Spectra: The optimizer tracks consecutive_rejects. If a spectrum's cost fails to improve for 15 consecutive iterations (despite damping adjustments), it is marked as converged (stuck) to prevent it from holding back the rest of the batch. This threshold (MAX_REJECTS in optimizer.py) can be adjusted if needed.

docs.title: 9.3. Damping Schedule
docs.text:
The per-spectrum damping factor \(\lambda\) is initialized at 1e-2 and adjusted after each iteration:

Outcome λ Adjustment Effect Cost improved λ /= 3.0 (floor 1e-10) Trust the Gauss-Newton direction more Cost worsened λ *= 2.5 (ceiling 1e10) Shift toward gradient descent

docs.title: 10. Noise Level Estimation and Noise Threshold
docs.text: The coef_noise parameter controls a noise-aware filtering system that can significantly improve both the performance and precision of fitting, especially on hyperspectral maps where many pixels may contain weak or absent peaks.

docs.title: 10.1. How Noise Level Is Estimated
docs.text:
Both the public detect_noise_level() helper (fit_engine/noise.py, used by the UI to display/report the noise level on the spectra viewer) and the internal batched estimator used during fitting (VBFevaluator.compute_noise_stats(), VBFthread._prepare_weights()) use the same robust estimator: the median absolute value of the first difference, rescaled to a Gaussian-equivalent sigma.

def detect_noise_level(y: np.ndarray) -> float:
    dy = np.diff(y)                                    # δ[i] = y[i+1] − y[i]
    return np.median(np.abs(dy)) / 0.6745 * np.sqrt(2)

Why this works:

Term Purpose np.diff(y) Point-to-point differences — dominated by noise, since real spectral features are broad and change slowly relative to one sample step np.median(np.abs(dy)) Median absolute difference — robust to the occasional large jump at a sharp peak edge, unlike a plain standard deviation / 0.6745 Converts a Gaussian median-absolute-deviation into an equivalent standard deviation (0.6745 = the MAD-to-σ constant for a normal distribution) * sqrt(2) A first difference of two independent noisy samples has variance \(2\sigma^2\); this rescales back to the per-point noise σ

VBFevaluator.compute_noise_stats(Y, coef_noise) applies the same diff/median logic along axis=1 to estimate one noise level per spectrum simultaneously across the whole map, and additionally computes a 5-point moving average of the signal (ymean) used to decide, point-by-point, whether the signal itself — not just the noise — is above the floor:

dy = np.diff(Y, axis=1)
ampli_noise = np.median(np.abs(dy), axis=1) / 0.6745 * np.sqrt(2)      # (N,)
Y_padded = np.pad(Y, ((0, 0), (2, 2)), mode='edge')
ymean = (Y_padded[:, 0:-4] + Y_padded[:, 1:-3] + Y_padded[:, 2:-2]
         + Y_padded[:, 3:-1] + Y_padded[:, 4:]) / 5.0                   # 5-point moving average
noise_level = coef_noise * ampli_noise                                   # (N,)

apply_noise_threshold() is called twice per fit (before and after optimization — see §5.2), and both calls need the exact same ymean/noise_level. VBFengine.fit_spectra() computes them once via compute_noise_stats() and passes the result (noise_stats=) to both calls, instead of repeating the median/smoothing pass twice (§2).

docs.title: 10.2. How coef_noise Activates Noise Thresholding
docs.text: When coef_noise > 0, a noise level threshold is computed as noise_level = coef_noise × ampli_noise. This threshold activates two complementary mechanisms:

docs.title: 10.2.1. Mechanism A — Weight Masking (VBFthread._prepare_weights)
docs.text:
Before the fit starts, any data point where the smoothed signal (ymean) falls below the noise level has its weight set to zero:

weights[ymean < noise_level[:, None]] = 0.0   # zero weight → ignored by optimizer

The optimizer's residual calculation \(\mathbf{r} = \mathbf{W} \circ (\mathbf{Y}_{pred} - \mathbf{Y}_{data})\) naturally ignores these masked points, so the fit focuses only on regions with meaningful signal.

docs.title: 10.2.2. Mechanism B — Peak Suppression (VBFevaluator.apply_noise_threshold)
docs.text:
Any peak whose center position (x0) falls in a below-threshold region has its amplitude and FWHM forced to zero; other shape parameters for that peak are restored to their pre-fit initial guess (p0_matrix) to prevent random fluctuations from being mapped as real structure. This runs twice during the pipeline (§5.2):

  1. Before optimization — sets a clean initial guess, preventing the optimizer from trying to fit noise fluctuations as peaks.
  2. After optimization — cleans up any peaks that may have drifted into noise regions during the LM iterations.

docs.title: 10.3.1. Performance
docs.text: Aspect How It Helps Faster convergence Zeroed-out peaks in noise regions start and stay at zero, effectively reducing the active parameter count Fewer wasted iterations Without noise masking, the optimizer spends many iterations fitting random noise with tiny ghost peaks Better initial guess Pre-zeroing noise-region peaks brings \(p_0\) closer to the true solution, so LM converges in fewer iterations

docs.title: 10.3.2. Precision
docs.text: Aspect How It Helps Eliminates ghost peaks In maps, some pixels have weak or absent peaks. Without thresholding, noise fluctuations are fitted as tiny false peaks, producing artifacts in parameter maps Stabilizes correlated parameters Near the noise floor, amplitude, width, and position become highly correlated — small noise perturbations cause large parameter swings. Suppression avoids this instability Prevents cross-talk A ghost peak in a noise region can "steal" intensity from a real neighboring peak, biasing its fitted amplitude. Suppression prevents this Cleaner R² values Masked noise regions do not contribute to the R² calculation, so the reported goodness-of-fit reflects only meaningful signal regions

docs.title: 10.4. Practical Example
docs.text:
Consider a Raman map with 3 defined peaks, where for some pixels peak #2 sits in a flat baseline region:

Without coef_noise (= 0):
  Peak #2 → ampli = 0.3 (noise artifact), fwhm = 2.1 (meaningless), x0 = 520.3 (drifted)
  Peak #1 → ampli = 18.2 (slightly biased — peak #2 stealing intensity)

With coef_noise = 1:
  Peak #2 → ampli = 0.0, fwhm = 0.0   (correctly suppressed)
  Peak #1 → ampli = 19.1              (accurate, no cross-talk)

docs.title: 10.5. Choosing the Right coef_noise Value
docs.text:
Value Behavior 0 Disabled — all peaks are fitted everywhere, no noise masking 0.5 – 1.0 Conservative — only suppresses peaks/regions well below the noise floor 1.0 – 2.0 Moderate — good default for most datasets 3.0 – 5.0 Aggressive — may suppress real weak peaks; use with caution > 5.0 Very aggressive — only strong, unambiguous peaks survive

The default value in MSettings.load_fit_settings() is 0.0 (disabled). The Settings UI exposes it as a spin box with range [0.0, 10.0] and step 0.5.

docs.title: 11.1. Fast Path: Analytical Jacobian (Recommended)
docs.text:
To add a new peak shape with maximum performance:

Step 1 — Define the batched evaluation function in models.py (with optional out=None buffer reuse):

def batched_newshape(x, params, out=None):
    """
    x:      (M,) or (N, M)
    params: (N, n_p) where columns are [param1, param2, ...]
    out:    optional (N, M) preallocated array
    Returns: (N, M)
    """
    p1 = params[:, 0:1]    # (N, 1) — broadcasts over M
    p2 = params[:, 1:2]
    if x.ndim == 1:
        dx = x[None, :] - p2    # (N, M)
    else:
        dx = x - p2
    result = p1 * some_function(dx)
    if out is not None:
        out[...] = result
        return out
    return result

Step 2 — Derive and define the analytical Jacobian (accepting out=None for slice-in-place evaluation):

def batched_newshape_jac(x, params, out=None):
    """Returns: (N, M, n_p) — partial derivatives w.r.t. each parameter."""
    # ... compute intermediates ...
    N, M = result.shape
    J = np.empty((N, M, n_p), dtype=np.float64) if out is None else out
    J[:, :, 0] = d_result_d_p1
    J[:, :, 1] = d_result_d_p2
    return J

Step 3 — Register in the BATCHED_MODELS dictionary:

BATCHED_MODELS = {
    # ... existing ...
    "NewShape": (batched_newshape, batched_newshape_jac, ["param1", "param2", ...]),
}

When deriving the Jacobian, follow the efficiency pattern used throughout models.py (§2.4, §7.1): compute any repeated 1/w-style term once as a reciprocal and reuse it, and prefer in-place ops (*=, +=) for large (N,M) intermediates. Validate the analytical Jacobian against numerical_jacobian() on random parameter sets before relying on it.

docs.title: 11.2. Slow Path: Scalar Fallback
docs.text:
If deriving an analytical Jacobian is impractical:

Step 1 — Define a scalar function in scalar_models.py:

def newshape(x, param1, param2):
    """x is a 1D array, params are scalars. Returns 1D array."""
    return param1 * some_function(x - param2)

Step 2 — Register in PEAK_MODEL_REGISTRY:

PEAK_MODEL_REGISTRY = {
    # ... existing ...
    "NewShape": (newshape, ["param1", "param2"]),
}

The evaluator will automatically wrap it via _make_batched_scalar() and use numerical_jacobian(). This is functional but significantly slower (~10–50× per peak per iteration).

docs.title: 11.3. Registration in the Application
docs.text:
After adding the model to the engine, register it in spectroview/__init__.py:

PEAK_MODELS = [
    "Gaussian", "Lorentzian", "PseudoVoigt",
    # ... existing ...
    "NewShape",  # Add here to appear in the UI dropdown
]

docs.title: 12. Timing and Diagnostics
docs.text:
The VBFengine records wall-clock timings for each step in self.timings:

Step 3 - build p0:     0.003s
Step 4 - batch fit:   1.234s (0.6 ms/spectrum, 1950/2000 converged)
Step 5 - write_back:   0.089s

Only these three entries are populated by VBFengine.fit_spectra() itself — the numbering starts at 3 because it continues from the (unrelated) upstream stages that happen before the engine is even called: model application to MapData and SpectraStore.batch_preprocess() (range crop + baseline subtraction), which are timed separately and documented in spectra_store.md.

These timings are emitted via VBFthread.timings_ready and printed to the console (set print_benchmark=True on fit_spectra() for live prints during debugging). They are invaluable for diagnosing performance bottlenecks:

  • If Step 4 dominates → normal; this is the actual optimization, and by far the largest cost for any non-trivial map.
  • If Step 4 shows low convergence → check initial guesses, bounds, or model suitability rather than performance.
  • If Step 3 or Step 5 are unexpectedly large relative to Step 4 → worth profiling; for typical maps they should be one to two orders of magnitude smaller than Step 4.

docs.title: 12.1. R² Computation
docs.text:
The goodness-of-fit metric R² is computed during build_results_batch():

\[ R^2 = 1 - \frac{\sum_i w_i (y_i - \hat{y}_i)^2}{\sum_i w_i (y_i - \bar{y}_w)^2} \]

Where \(\bar{y}_w\) is the weighted mean. When weights are present, only non-zero-weight points contribute to both the numerator and denominator, ensuring that masked regions (negative values, noise-floor points) do not artificially inflate or deflate the reported quality.

docs.title: Technically Validated Specification & Implementation Roadmap: Multi-Map Selection & Live Maps
docs.text:
Document Status: Audited, Performance-Validated & Implementation-Ready Specification Supersedes: Draft Roadmap (34431df, initial Phases 1–4 proposal) Primary Modules Affected:

  • spectroview/model/spectra_store.py, spectroview/model/spectral_parameters.py
  • spectroview/viewmodel/vm_workspace_maps.py, spectroview/viewmodel/vm_workspace_spectra.py, spectroview/viewmodel/vm_live_maps.py
  • spectroview/view/components/v_map_list.py, spectroview/view/components/v_live_maps.py, spectroview/view/v_workspace_maps.py, spectroview/view/v_workspace_spectra.py

Related Features: Multi-Map Selection, RGB Spectral Range Brackets (VSpectraViewer / RangeSelectorManager), Adaptive 1D/2D Live Maps, Green Red/Blue (R/B) Ratio, Vectorized Parameter Caching

docs.title: 1. Executive Summary
docs.text:
This document presents a comprehensive technical re-audit and implementation-ready specification for adding multi-map selection in the Maps workspace while hardening the RGB Live Brackets, Adaptive 1D/2D Live Maps, and Green R/B Ratio subsystems for large hyperspectral workloads.

A second, code- and benchmark-driven audit of the existing codebase and the initial roadmap (34431df) exposed critical architectural contradictions, stale-state bugs, silent signal amplification, and severe CPU/memory bottlenecks:

  1. Unreported 2× and Spurious Recomputations: Under current wiring, switching maps computes Live Maps twice (6 parameter passes across 3 brackets), single-point clicks in VMapViewer trigger full-map recalculation (3 spurious passes), and checkbox toggles recompute all channels even though VMLiveMaps ignores MapData.is_active. Multi-selecting \(K\) maps would multiply this wasted work by \(K\times\).
  2. Invalidated < 15 ms Performance Claim: Direct benchmarking shows a single 3,721-spectrum map already takes 39.1–40.8 ms in VMLiveMaps compute alone, while N = 90,000 allocates 947.5 MB peak Python memory and takes 1.37–1.54 s due to casting the entire (N, M) matrix from float32 to float64 before column-masking. Scattered 2D maps re-run scipy.interpolate.griddata from scratch on every drag tick (209.7 ms at N = 2,401; 14.51 s at N = 160,000), and Matplotlib Agg redraws cost 127.6–188.7 ms per subpanel (~380–566 ms across 3 subpanels).
  3. Unresolved UX & Data Contracts: The prior proposal contradicted itself on multi-map bulk preprocessing scope and mixed 1D/2D precedence, omitted VMapsList placeholder/selection Qt traps, left workspace-clear stale references unhandled, and omitted R/B ratio invalidation and heterogeneous map axis bounds.

docs.title: Resolved Design Baseline
docs.text: Ambiguity / Risk in Prior Draft (34431df) Validated Specification Decision Bulk operations scope (Section 4.A Primary-only vs. Phase 2 _get_target_mds multi-select) Strict Primary-Only for all preprocessing, baseline, peak-model, fit, and single-map export tools (Ctrl-to-apply-all behavior preserved). Multi-selection drives comparison in Live Maps (plus explicit multi-map Delete confirmation on sidebar removal). Mixed 1D + 2D selection (Section 4.D Primary-precedence vs. Phase 3 all(...) 1D) Primary-Precedence Mode Selection: Primary map (current_map_name) dimensionality sets Live Maps mode (1D compares all selected 1D profiles; 2D enters 2D comparison switcher). Excluded mismatched maps are never coerced; an explicit exclusion badge informs the user. 2D multi-map comparison UX (per-subpanel combo vs. tab-level switcher vs. micro-grid) Single Tab-Level 2D Switcher (Prev / Combo / Next in VLiveMaps header), initialized to Primary Map so Red, Blue, and Green (R/B) always inspect the same coherent 2D map. Multi-profile legend crowding (per-subpanel ax.legend() on 250 px axes) Single Shared Tab-Level Header Legend Strip in VLiveMaps (only shown when \(\ge 2\) profiles are plotted), preserving 100% of plot axis area. RGB brackets across differing X ranges (per-map brackets vs. shared brackets) Shared Workspace Brackets positioned on Primary Map's VSpectraViewer. Comparison maps missing points inside [x_min, x_max] yield NaN (with a concise partial/no-overlap status indicator) rather than silently hiding mismatches behind independent intervals. Large map latency & UI freezes (full-matrix float64, repeated griddata, hidden-tab eager work) Phase 0 Prerequisites: Visibility-gated lazy evaluation, clean signal separation, slice-first float64 casting, cached Delaunay barycentric weights for scattered 2D maps, explicit MapData.data_version cache invalidation, and adaptive drag coalescing (plus optional thresholded QThreadPool worker for massive batches in Phase 5).

docs.title: 2. Phase I — Critical Re-Audit of the Initial Proposal (34431df)
docs.text: The prior document (docs/roadmaps/multi_map_selection_live_maps.md, revision 34431df) correctly identified the Two-Tier Selection concept (Primary Active Map vs. Selected Maps Group), but failed validation across five critical areas when checked against SPECTROview source code and empirical benchmarks.

docs.title: A. Internal Architectural Contradictions
docs.text:
1. Contradiction on Bulk Operations Scope:
  2. Draft Section 1 & Section 4.A: Explicitly promised "All single-map tools (VMapViewer, VSpectraViewer, VMoreTab, VFitModelBuilder, VMVA, btn_view, btn_save) operate exclusively on the Primary Active Map."
  3. Draft Phase 2 Step 1: Prescribes "Update _get_target_mds(apply_all) to target selected_map_names when multiple are selected."

  4. Why this is dangerous: Source inspection of spectroview/viewmodel/vm_workspace_maps.py shows _get_target_mds() (lines 449–455) only serves 7 actions (reinit_spectra, apply_spectral_range, paste_baseline, subtract_baseline, delete_baseline, paste_peaks, delete_peaks) and is bypassed by apply_y_normalization / undo_y_normalization (which resolve targets via _get_selected_spectra()), apply_x_correction / undo_x_correction, _apply_fit_model_and_run, fit, _run_fit_thread, delete_current_map, and CSV saving. Making _get_target_mds() silently mutate selected_map_names would cause asymmetric destructive edits across half the toolbar when a user selects maps purely to overlay Live Maps.

  5. Contradiction on Mixed 1D/2D Multi-Selection:

  6. Draft Section 4.D: "If the Primary Map is a 1D profile, Live Maps plots all selected 1D profiles (ignoring 2D maps with a status badge: 'Comparing 2 profile(s); 1 2D map excluded')."
  7. Draft Phase 3 Step 2: "If all selected maps are 1D profiles (all(analyze_map_geometry(md.coords).is_profile for md in mds)): ... If 2D maps: prioritize primary map."
  8. Those two rules produce opposite results whenever a user selects [Profile_1D (Primary), Wafer_2D]: Section 4.D plots Profile_1D as a line plot, whereas Phase 3 Step 2 sees all(...) == False and prioritizes the Primary... which is 1D, leaving an unhandled fallthrough branch.

docs.title: B. Invalidated Performance Assumptions
docs.text:
Draft Section 4.E claimed: "Calculating parameters across multiple large maps (e.g., three 3,721-point maps = 11,163 spectra) during live bracket dragging is kept fluid (< 15 ms total)."

Direct benchmark runs against HEAD (34431df) disprove this assumption across every stage of the pipeline:

Operation / Benchmark Scenario (Observed on 34431df) Measured Latency Measured Peak Alloc Prior Claim Verdict compute_spectral_parameter (10% band, M = 1015), N = 3,721 29.7 ms 39.2 MB "< 15 ms for 3 maps" Refuted (1 map > 2× budget) VMLiveMaps full pass (R+B+G R/B, 1 map N = 3,721) 39.1–40.8 ms — "< 15 ms for 3 maps" Refuted (3× ~120 ms compute) compute_spectral_parameter, N = 90,000 (Y0 float32 = 365.4 MB) 732.2 ms 947.5 MB Unanalyzed Critical Memory Spike VMLiveMaps full pass (1 map N = 90,000) 1,366.9–1,538.6 ms — Unanalyzed 1.5 s UI Stall compute_map_grid (scattered N = 2,401 / N = 160,000) 209.7 ms / 14,507.3 ms — Unanalyzed 14.5 s UI Freeze LiveMapSubpanel Agg render+draw (320×260, 2,000-pt 1D / 300×300 2D) 127.6 ms / 188.7 ms — "fluid" 380–566 ms across 3 panels

The draft completely missed Matplotlib Agg canvas draw cost (~128–189 ms per subpanel = ~380–566 ms per 3-panel update), which exceeds the 60 ms debounce timer by 6×–9×.

docs.title: C. Overlooked Redundant Compute & Lifecycle Bugs
docs.text:
Instrumentation of the current signal graph (3 active brackets) quantified severe existing compute waste before multi-selection is even added:

  • Map switch via VMapsList: Fires batches = 2, compute_calls = 6, panel_updates = 6 (2× redundant) because VMWorkspaceMaps.select_map() (lines 117–138) emits both spectra_selection_changed and map_data_updated, and VWorkspaceMaps routes both to vm_live_maps.set_map_data(md).
  • Clicking a single spectrum point in VMapViewer: Fires batches = 1, compute_calls = 3, panel_update_map = 3 (100% spurious). Selecting a spectrum point changes no map intensities, yet _on_map_viewer_selection emits spectra_selection_changed, forcing a full-map recompute of all 3 Live Maps channels.
  • Toggling a spectrum checkbox (is_active): Fires batches = 1, compute_calls = 3, panel_update_map = 3, even though VMLiveMaps computes across the entire md.y_matrix without consulting md.is_active.
  • Hidden-tab eager computation: Neither VWorkspaceSpectra nor VWorkspaceMaps checks whether Live Maps is the active tab in bottom_tabs. Loading maps, preprocessing, or clicking heatmap points computes and draws all 3 hidden Matplotlib canvases synchronously.
  • Workspace clear & last-map delete memory leak: VWorkspaceMaps._on_map_data_changed() (line 396) guards if self.vm.current_map_name: before calling set_map_data. Clearing the workspace (clear_workspace) or deleting the final map never notifies VMLiveMaps, leaving the deleted MapData pinned in VMLiveMaps._current_md and stale plots rendered.
  • Bracket toggle double-evaluation & missing label sync: VWorkspaceSpectra._on_range_selector_toggled() (lines 393–401) sets the range (_timer.start()) and immediately calls set_selector_active(..., True) (synchronous recompute), triggering two passes when a bracket turns on. Additionally, VWorkspaceSpectra.setup_connections() does not connect selector_state_changed, leaving LiveMapSubpanel header range badges potentially out of sync on axis initialization.

docs.title: D. Overlooked Qt ExtendedSelection & VMapsList Implementation Traps
docs.text:
Draft Phase 1 prescribed "Enable ExtendedSelection; emit Signal(list, str)" without inspecting spectroview/view/components/v_map_list.py internals:

  1. 5 Non-Map Placeholder Rows: When empty, _update_maps_placeholder() (v_map_list.py:136–154) inserts 4 spacer QListWidgetItems + 1 text prompt with Qt.NoItemFlags. Naive count(), setCurrentRow(0), or index math collides with placeholder rows unless filtered cleanly (unlike VSpectraList, which tracks real items cleanly and cleans spacer flags).
  2. Row-Index Selection Restoration: VMapsList.set_maps_names() (lines 157–177) currently preserves selection by integer row index rather than map name, and VWorkspaceMaps._on_map_data_changed() calls self.v_maps_list.set_selected_map_name(self.vm.current_map_name) (line 376), which executes setCurrentRow(). Under ExtendedSelection, calling setCurrentRow(row) without QItemSelectionModel.NoUpdate clears all other selected rows and destroys multi-selection on every preprocessing step or map addition.
  3. currentItem() vs. selectedItems() Divergence: In Qt ExtendedSelection:
  4. Ctrl+Click on the currently focused item deselects it from selectedItems() while leaving currentItem() pointing at the now-unselected item.
  5. Clicking empty viewport whitespace clears selectedItems() to [], while currentItem() may still reference the last focused item.
  6. The draft did not define reconciliation rules for primary_name vs. selected_names.
  7. Unsafe Qt Signal Signature: Signal(list, str) cannot cleanly carry None when the workspace is cleared (None coerces to "" or triggers PySide6 signature edge cases). Signal(list, object) (emitting list[str] and Optional[str]) matches safe None semantics.

docs.title: E. Visualization, Ratio Semantics & Testing Deficiencies
docs.text:
• Legend Crowding: Calling self.ax.legend() inside a ~250–300 px Figure(layout="compressed") shrinks Matplotlib's layout engine around tick labels and titles across all 3 subpanels identically.
  • Unaddressed R/B Edge Cases & Cache Invalidation: Draft Phase 3 step 3 gave one line to _compute_rb_ratio(), ignoring cross-map non-overlapping ranges, all-NaN heatmaps (nanmin/nanmax), Red-change \(\rightarrow\) Green invalidation, and MapData in-place array mutations (where _intensity_cache keyed by Python id(md) or array identity would risk stale hits if mutated in place, e.g., apply_cosmic_ray_erase).
  • Testing Separation Violation: Draft Section 7 proposed testing VMapsList widget behavior inside tests/unit/viewmodel/test_vm_workspace_maps.py, conflating View widget tests (tests/unit/view/test_v_maps_list.py) with headless ViewModel tests.

    VM-->>V: map_data_updated()
    V->>VLM: set_map_data(mdB) [Compute Pass #2: DUPLICATE 3 channels]
    VLM-->>Sub: update_map / update_profile_data (3 more Agg draws)

    Note over User,Sub: Current Bug 2: Point click in VMapViewer triggers spurious full recompute
    User->>V: Click 1 point on heatmap
    V->>VM: selected_fnames = [point_fname]
    VM-->>V: spectra_selection_changed([point_fname])
    V->>VLM: set_map_data(mdB) [Spurious Compute Pass: 3 channels]

docs.title: 4. Phase III — Identified Limitations & Missing Considerations
4.1 Architecture & State Management
docs.text:
1. Conflated Signal Semantics: spectra_selection_changed means two completely different things in Maps workspace: "spectra highlighted inside the current map" (VMapViewer point click) vs. "active map context changed" (VMWorkspaceMaps.select_map). Routing spectra_selection_changed to Live Maps in VWorkspaceMaps._on_selection_changed_for_live_maps (lines 229–234) causes both duplicate map-switch passes and spurious point-click passes. Note that in VWorkspaceSpectra (setup_connections, lines 277–286), spectra_selection_changed rightly feeds Live Maps in "series" mode because highlighted items are the selected 1D spectra; VWorkspaceMaps must override that route cleanly.
  2. Primary-vs-Selected Invariant: When multiple maps are selected in VMapsList:
  3. Single-map state (current_map_name, current_map_df, selected_fnames, VMapViewer, VMapViewerDialogs, VSpectraViewer, VFitModelBuilder, vm_mva, VMoreTab, application/service.py::get_active_map()) remains strictly coupled to Primary Active Map.
  4. Comparison state (selected_map_names: list[str], deduplicated in list order) routes read-only references (SpectraStore.get_map_data(name)) to VMLiveMaps. Zero deep-copying of Y0 or Y occurs across selection changes.
  5. Mutating vs. Viewing Map Data: Preprocessing operations (apply_y_normalization, subtract_baseline, apply_spectral_range, apply_x_correction, apply_cosmic_ray_erase) and VBF fit completion mutate MapData arrays (Y, x, peak_params, fit_r2, Y_bestfit). Today there is no version counter on MapData, preventing cross-batch reuse of per-map bracket integrals or geometry caches without risking stale reads after in-place mutations.

docs.title: Root-Cause Bottlenecks Identified
docs.text:
1. Full-Matrix Upcast in spectral_parameters.py:116: y_arr = np.asarray(Y, dtype=np.float64) runs before the spectral band mask (lines 135–142) trims columns down to the 5–15% range under the bracket. Copying 365.4 MB float32 into 730.8 MB float64 (plus intermediate temporaries = 947.5 MB) creates severe memory pressure and cache thrashing; across 5 multi-selected large maps this risks multi-GB stalls or OOM on 32-bit/laptop environments. Masking columns before casting (np.asarray(Y[:, mask], dtype=np.float64)) cuts intermediate allocation by \(\approx 10\times\) and measured slice+cast time by \(\approx 4\times\).
  2. Repeated scipy.interpolate.griddata on Scattered Maps: Every 60 ms bracket move on a non-orthogonal wafer map rebuilds a 2D Qhull Delaunay triangulation and barycentric search from scratch (209.7 ms for 50×50; 14.5 s for 400×400). Because (X, Y) spatial coordinates do not change during bracket drags, Delaunay simplex indices and vertex weights are strictly invariant per map geometry and can be precomputed once and applied in < 1 ms per bracket tick.
  3. Matplotlib Agg Redraw Budget & Bracket Drag Churn: Each full 3-subpanel Agg draw takes ~383 ms (1D) to ~566 ms (2D), while RangeSelectorManager.render(ax) (v_range_selector.py:282–366) removes and recreates 7 artists on every canvas mouse-motion event (v_spectra_viewer.py:2584–2593). A fixed 60 ms QTimer fires faster than Matplotlib finishes drawing large maps, queueing back-to-back main-thread stalls.
  4. Inactive Tab Execution: Computing and drawing Live Maps while bottom_tabs is showing Fit Model Builder, Fit Results, or MVA is pure waste.
  5. is_active Consistency Gap: VMapViewer omits unchecked spectra (is_active == False) via get_current_map_dataframe(), whereas VMLiveMaps evaluates all N rows directly from md.y_matrix—yet set_spectrum_active / set_all_current_map_spectra_active emit map_data_updated, causing 3 full recomputes whose pixel output doesn't even reflect the unchecked mask! Live Maps should either consistently mask inactive pixels (NaN for 2D grids / omit or break 1D points—or explicitly match VMapViewer semantics via is_active masking in vectorized NumPy) and cache cleanly. Using is_active directly via vectorized masking (~md.is_active -> NaN after fast vectorized intensity slice, or slicing active rows Y[active, mask]) guarantees 1:1 visual fidelity with VMapViewer without copying DataFrames.

docs.title: 4.3 RGB Live Brackets & Green R/B Ratio Semantics
docs.text:
1. Bracket Range Compatibility Across Multiple Maps: Maps loaded together may span different spectral ranges (e.g., 100–1800 cm^-1 vs. 400–1200 cm^-1, or 532 nm vs. 633 nm calibration). When a Red or Blue bracket [x_min, x_max] has \(< 1\) (or \(< 2\) for trapezoidal integration) wavenumber samples in comparison Map \(j\):
  2. Map \(j\) must not crash (ValueError: zero-size array or IndexError) and must not silently plot 0.0.
  3. compute_spectral_parameter / VMLiveMaps must return an all-NaN array for that channel on Map \(j\), exclude all-NaN curves from autoscale bounds cleanly, and annotate the subpanel status badge (e.g., "Map B: out of spectral range").
  4. R/B Ratio Dependency & Numerical Edge Cases:
  5. In VMLiveMaps._recalculate_batch, when Green parameter is R/B ratio, changing Red or Blue must recalculate Green, reusing Red and Blue 1D intensity vectors computed in the same pass via _intensity_cache (keyed by (id(md), md.data_version, color_id, round(x_min, 6), round(x_max, 6), active_digest)).
  6. If Red or Blue is deactivated or yields empty range / near-zero denominator (abs(I_blue) < max(abs(I_blue)) * 1e-3, matching compute_intensity_ratio at spectral_parameters.py:616–647), pixels/points with small I_blue become NaN. If all values are NaN, Matplotlib 2D normalization (np.nanmin/np.nanmax) would raise ValueError unless explicitly guarded (fall back to 0.0, 1.0 and show "No valid R/B points" message).
  7. Intensity cache must not survive across MapData preprocessing/baseline/fit changes: explicit MapData.data_version: int = 0 increments on any array or is_active mutation.
  8. Toggle & Init Sync:
  9. Fix VWorkspaceSpectra._on_range_selector_toggled (lines 393–401) so activating a bracket does not schedule both an async timer via set_selector_range(..., immediate=False) and a synchronous run via set_selector_active(..., True).
  10. Connect vm_live_maps.selector_state_changed in VWorkspaceSpectra.setup_connections() so programmatic range clamping/initialization immediately updates subpanel header [x_min, x_max] pills.

docs.title: 4.4 Multi-Map Selection & UX Edge Cases
docs.text:
1. ExtendedSelection Corner Cases in VMapsList:
  2. Placeholder isolation: _update_maps_placeholder() rows must be stripped on real population and ignored when reading selection/primary state (Qt.UserRole or tracked item set rather than raw row(item)).
  3. Ctrl-deselect of focused item: When currentItem() is no longer in selectedItems(), promote the top/last still-selected item as primary_name (or only update primary_name cleanly) so the Primary Map is always an actually selected map whenever len(selected_names) >= 1.
  4. Empty viewport click: Clicking blank whitespace clears selectedItems(). Guard against wiping current_map_name unexpectedly or explicitly handle empty selection (current_map_name = None, selected_map_names = [], Live Maps displays clean empty state — matching VSpectraList / empty workspace behavior cleanly, OR re-select previous if single-click empty area? Standard Qt ExtendedSelection like VSpectraList leaves empty selection cleanly; Live Maps and viewers must tolerate empty selection without errors).
  5. Programmatic preservation: set_maps_names() and _on_map_data_changed() must preserve selected_map_names by map name (QItemSelectionModel.Select) without clobbering selection via setCurrentRow().
  6. 1D Spatial Axis Labeling & Scale Fidelity:
  7. analyze_map_geometry(md.coords) extracts projected 1D positions, axis_label, and is_profile.
  8. When comparing multiple 1D profiles simultaneously:
    • If all share an X-aligned axis_label, use that shared X label cleanly.
    • If all share a Y-aligned axis_label, use that shared Y label cleanly.
    • If profiles mix X and Y directions or oblique traces -> plot each against its own positions, label the axis generically (e.g., "Position / Distance"), and note mixed axis orientations in the status badge.
  9. Aspect Ratio Regression Prevention: Switching 2D \(\rightarrow\) 1D (or switching between single 2D map and multi-1D selection) must always invoke LiveMapSubpanel._reset_axes() with self.ax.set_aspect("auto", adjustable="box") before plotting lines (preventing the squished-axis scale regression previously observed when 2D aspect lock persisted onto 1D line plots).
  10. Color Determinism & Visual Hierarchy:
  11. Assign colors sequentially from spectroview.__init__.DEFAULT_COLORS (20 high-contrast hex colors) paired with MARKERS fallback if \(> 20\) profiles are selected.
  12. Color/label assignment should follow deterministic selection order (or stable map-name-indexed mapping during a session) with Primary Map rendered at higher zorder and slightly heavier stroke (linewidth=2.0 vs 1.5) so users immediately spot the active map.
  13. 2D Multi-Map Comparison Ergonomics:
  14. Providing a tab-level [ < | Map Name Combo ▼ | > ] switcher bar in VLiveMaps allows comparing Red / Blue / R/B maps across all selected 2D maps without leaving Live Maps, keeping all 3 channels strictly locked to the same 2D map. Default selection in the switcher follows primary_map_name (unless user explicitly steps to a comparison map currently still in the selected 2D set).

docs.title: 4.5 Error Handling & Robustness
docs.text:
• Empty / N = 0 / N = 1 Maps: N = 0 emits empty payload clearing subpanel safely; N = 1 map has degenerate SVD spatial span—check analyze_map_geometry behavior (is_profile=False vs single-point series fallback) so compute_map_grid (0-span extent) never divides by zero or passes singular imshow bounds (x_min == x_max padded cleanly, already guarded or verified).
  • Non-Monotonic or Unsorted x_axis: Integrated intensity uses trapezoidal / sorted quadrature or assumes ascending/descending x_axis; if comparison map x_axis is descending (e.g., nm vs \(\text{cm}^{-1}\) or reversed export), compute_spectral_parameter sign normalization (abs or ascending sort check) must handle it uniformly across all maps.
  • Unmounted / Deleted Map References: Always resolve map names against SpectraStore before compute; strip removed names from selected_map_names and VMLiveMaps._current_mds immediately in remove_map() and clear_workspace().
  • Async Stale Write Guard: Any background QThreadPool calculation must validate a monotonic generation_id token before applying emitted arrays to VLiveMaps.

docs.title: Decision Matrix Across 7 Key Engineering Axes
docs.text: Design Axis Alternative A Alternative B Alternative C Adopted Choice & Rationale 1. Multi-Select Bulk Ops Scope Apply _get_target_mds() to selected_map_names Always Primary-only (keep Ctrl override for All maps; explicit confirmation on Multi-Delete) Dual toolbar toggle "Apply to Selected" Alternative B: Resolves the Section 4.A vs. Phase 2 contradiction cleanly, maintains 100% consistency across all preprocessing/fitting actions (even those bypassing _get_target_mds()), and prevents accidental destructive edits during visual Live Maps comparison. 2. Mixed 1D/2D Precedence Require all() maps be 1D (all(...)) to show profiles Primary-Precedence Mode: Primary's dimensionality determines Live Maps display (1D compares all selected 1D; 2D enters 2D mode) + exclusion count Stack both 1D profiles and 2D heatmaps inside each subpanel Alternative B: Intuitive mental model ("what you focus on sets the mode"), zero vertical-height starvation, and explicit status feedback ("Comparing 2 1D profiles (1 2D map excluded)"). 3. 2D Multi-Map UX Tab-level shared [< \| Map ▼ \| >] switcher bar Independent combo box per subpanel Side-by-side tiled mini-heatmaps (~80 px each) Alternative A: Preserves ~250–300 px readable subpanel width, guarantees Red/Blue/Green(R/B) show the exact same 2D specimen, and lets users step through selected 2D maps in 1 click without changing VMapViewer. 4. Multi-Profile Legend Per-subpanel self.ax.legend() Single shared header legend strip in VLiveMaps (above the 3 subpanels, visible when \(\ge 2\) profiles) Interactive tooltip-only hover Alternative B: Calling ax.legend() on three layout="compressed" axes steals 20–35% plot area identically; a shared Qt badge strip costs zero Matplotlib layout budget and guarantees uniform styling. 5. RGB Bracket Ownership Shared brackets on Primary VSpectraViewer (out-of-range maps yield NaN + indicator) Per-map stored independent bracket intervals Union-clamped brackets across all maps Alternative A: Live comparison requires measuring the same spectral window across samples; independent brackets make R/B and intensity comparison physically ambiguous. 6. Scattered 2D Interpolation Re-run scipy.interpolate.griddata per drag tick (210 ms–14.5 s) Precompute & cache Delaunay simplex indices + barycentric weights per map coords (deferred scipy.spatial.Delaunay) Fixed coarse nearest-neighbor downsampling (cKDTree) Alternative B (plus cKDTree nearest fallback for collinear/1D-like scatter): Reproduces exact linear griddata output while turning drag ticks from 210 ms–14.5 s into < 1 ms vectorized indexing (O(grid^2)). Preserves deferred scipy import invariant. 7. Scheduling & Concurrency Sync coalesced main-thread only (60 ms timer) Always async QThreadPool for every map Hybrid: Phase 0/3 visibility gate + adaptive debounce (max(60 ms, last_ms)) + Phase 5 thresholded QThreadPool when sum(N_active) > 25,000 Alternative C: Avoids thread-handoff overhead & complexity for normal < 25k workloads while keeping UI smooth on 90k–160k+ maps or heavy multi-map selections. Matplotlib canvas draws stay strictly on Qt main thread.

docs.title: Phase 0: Baseline Hygiene, Memory/Interpolation Fixes & Lifecycle Bugs
A. Objective
docs.text: Eliminate existing duplicate computations, 947.5 MB memory spikes, 14.5 s scattered-interpolation freezes, hidden-tab CPU waste, and workspace-clear memory leaks before multi-selection multiplies these flaws by \(N\) selected maps.

docs.title: B. Files and Components
docs.text:
• spectroview/model/spectra_store.py (MapData)
  • spectroview/model/spectral_parameters.py (compute_spectral_parameter, compute_map_grid, new cached Delaunay helper)
  • spectroview/viewmodel/vm_workspace_maps.py, spectroview/viewmodel/vm_workspace_spectra.py
  • spectroview/view/v_workspace_maps.py, spectroview/view/v_workspace_spectra.py
  • spectroview/viewmodel/vm_live_maps.py

docs.title: C. Technical Implementation
docs.text:
1. MapData.data_version: int = 0 (spectra_store.py):
  2. Add data_version: int = 0 and helper def touch(self) -> None: self.data_version += 1 to MapData.
  3. Call md.touch() (or via SpectraStore / VMWorkspaceSpectra mutators) whenever x, Y, is_active, peak_params, fit_r2, Y_bestfit, or apply_cosmic_ray_erase modifies md.
  4. Slice-First float64 Cast (spectral_parameters.py):
  5. In compute_spectral_parameter(), construct the column boolean mask mask = (x_arr >= x_min) & (x_arr <= x_max) on x_arr before converting Y to float64: 
    # Slice columns FIRST on float32 view, then cast ONLY selected band to float64
y_band = np.asarray(Y[:, mask], dtype=np.float64)
  6. Handle descending x_arr cleanly so trapezoidal integration yields non-negative integral magnitude (respecting ascending order uniformly).
  7. Return np.full(Y.shape[0], np.nan, dtype=np.float64) if np.count_nonzero(mask) == 0 (or < 2 for trapezoidal mode when bracket width is smaller than step spacing — check single-point fallback cleanly).
  8. Cached Delaunay Barycentric Grid Interpolation (spectral_parameters.py / VMLiveMaps):
  9. Add a precomputed spatial gridder dataclass PrecomputedGridder (or helper build_map_gridder(coords, grid_res=80) and evaluate_map_grid(values, gridder)):
    • Keep from scipy.spatial import Delaunay strictly inside the helper function to satisfy startup import deferral (tests/performance/test_startup_imports.py).
    • Compute Delaunay triangulation once per unique (coords_shape, coords_bytes_hash_or_token) and extract per-grid-pixel simplex vertex indices (grid_res^2, 3) and barycentric weights (grid_res^2, 3) + out-of-hull mask (simplex == -1 -> NaN).
    • Fallback gracefully to regular 2D grid fast indexing when coordinates lie on a regular Cartesian lattice (preserving current 0.76–16.5 ms fast path) and to scipy.spatial.cKDTree nearest-neighbor if points are coplanar/collinear (QhullError).
    • Maintain backward compatibility of compute_map_grid(coords, values, grid_res=80, gridder=None) optional parameter.
  10. Signal Separation & Tab-Visibility Gate (vm_workspace_maps.py, v_workspace_maps.py, v_workspace_spectra.py):
  11. Stop calling vm_live_maps.set_map_data(md) inside VWorkspaceMaps._on_selection_changed_for_live_maps (v_workspace_maps.py:229–234)! Map-point clicks in VMapViewer emit spectra_selection_changed only for VSpectraViewer, never triggering full-map Live Maps recalculation.
  12. Route Live Maps updates strictly from map-level events (_on_map_data_changed, map selection change) using a single consolidated pass (reducing 2 -> 1 batches per map switch).
  13. Add visibility gating in VWorkspaceSpectra and VWorkspaceMaps: track self._live_maps_dirty: bool = False; if self.bottom_tabs.currentWidget() is not self.v_live_maps, store dirty state and return without calling vm_live_maps recalculation; connect self.bottom_tabs.currentChanged to flush dirty updates once when the user opens Live Maps.
  14. Fix _on_range_selector_toggled (v_workspace_spectra.py:393–401) so activating a bracket does not double-calculate synchronously AND asynchronously; connect vm_live_maps.selector_state_changed in VWorkspaceSpectra.setup_connections().
  15. Clean Clear & Empty-State Lifecycle (v_workspace_maps.py, vm_live_maps.py):
  16. Remove the if self.vm.current_map_name: guard skipping Live Maps reset in _on_map_data_changed() (v_workspace_maps.py:396). When current_map_name is None (workspace cleared or final map deleted), call vm_live_maps.set_map_data(None) (or set_map_datas([])), stop _timer, clear _pending_calc, _intensity_cache, _geometry_cache, and reset all 3 LiveMapSubpanel instances.

docs.text: None (independent prerequisite phase).

docs.title: E. Performance Considerations
docs.text:
• Cuts N = 90,000 peak compute memory from 947.5 MB to ~110 MB and slice+cast time by ~4×.
  • Cuts scattered N = 160,000 drag tick compute from 14,507 ms to < 2 ms after initial triangulation.
  • Cuts idle hidden-tab and point-click computes to 0.

docs.title: F. Edge Cases
docs.text:
• Collinear/degenerate coordinates raising scipy.spatial.QhullError in Delaunay -> fallback to cKDTree or single-point handling.
  • In-place Y edit (cosmic ray erase) forgetting md.touch() -> ensure all mutators in VMWorkspaceSpectra and VMWorkspaceMaps bump data_version.
  • bottom_tabs index changed programmatically in tests -> verify isVisible() vs currentWidget() is self.v_live_maps carefully so headless unit tests that test VMLiveMaps directly bypass View-layer tab gating cleanly, and View-layer integration tests trigger bottom_tabs.setCurrentWidget(ws.v_live_maps).

docs.title: G. Testing and Validation
docs.text:
• tests/unit/model/test_spectral_parameters.py: Verify slice-first output matches full-matrix float64 output to < 1e-12 relative tolerance; verify empty-mask NaN return; verify build_map_gridder matches griddata(..., method="linear") and handles collinear QhullError.
  • tests/unit/viewmodel/test_vm_live_maps.py: Verify data_version invalidates cache; set_map_data(None) clears state and stops timer.
  • tests/unit/view/test_workspace_maps_live_wiring.py: Spy on VMLiveMaps recalculations proving point-click = 0 passes, map switch = 1 pass, hidden tab = 0 passes followed by 1 flush on tab switch, clear workspace resets panels.
  • tests/performance/test_startup_imports.py: Verify zero new top-level scipy imports.

docs.title: H. Acceptance Criteria
docs.text:
• Map switch runs exactly 1 compute batch (down from 2); point click runs 0 batches; hidden tab runs 0 batches.
  • N = 90,000 compute_spectral_parameter peak Python allocation reduced by \(\ge 75\%\).
  • Scattered N = 2,401 and 160,000 drag ticks run in \(< 5\text{ ms}\) post-init.

docs.text: • spectroview/view/components/v_map_list.py (VMapsList)

docs.title: C. Technical Implementation
docs.text:
1. Selection Mode & Placeholder Hygiene:
  2. Switch self.maps_list.setSelectionMode(QAbstractItemView.ExtendedSelection) (replacing SingleSelection at line 73).
  3. Store the real map name in item.setData(Qt.UserRole, map_name) (or track an explicit self._is_placeholder_active: bool / item.flags() & Qt.ItemIsSelectable) so the 5 placeholder rows from _update_maps_placeholder() (lines 136–154) are never confused with real map items.

A. Objective

docs.title: C. Technical Implementation
docs.text:
1. Multi-Map Entrypoint & Mode State:
  2. Add set_map_datas(self, mds: list[MapData], primary_name: Optional[str] = None, active_2d_name: Optional[str] = None):
    • Keep set_map_data(self, md: Optional[MapData]) as a thin wrapper (self.set_map_datas([md], md.name) if md is not None else self.set_map_datas([])).
    • Store self._current_mds: list[MapData], self._primary_map_name: Optional[str], and self._active_2d_map_name: Optional[str] (for 2D switcher control; initialized/re-anchored to primary_name if the previously viewed 2D map was deselected or Primary changed).
    • Add set_active_2d_map(self, map_name: str) to switch which selected 2D map is displayed on demand without re-selecting in VMapsList.
  3. When not mds: stop _timer, clear _pending_calc, clear _intensity_cache, emit empty reset signal (live_maps_cleared or empty series/profile payload), and return immediately.
  4. Primary-Precedence Dimensionality Classification:
  5. Classify each map's spatial geometry via cached (id(md), md.coords_version_or_shape) analyze_map_geometry(md.coords).
  6. Determine Primary Map primary_md:
    • If primary_md.is_profile (1D Mode):
    • Included targets: [md for md in mds if geom[md].is_profile].
    • Excluded count: n_excluded_2d = len(mds) - len(included) (included in status telemetry, e.g., "Comparing 3 1D profiles (1 2D map excluded)").
    • Else (2D Mode):
    • Included 2D candidates: [md for md in mds if not geom[md].is_profile].
    • Active displayed map: target_2d = by_name.get(self._active_2d_map_name) or primary_md.
    • Emit switcher metadata (available_2d_names, active_2d_name, n_excluded_1d) and evaluate intensities ONLY for target_2d (do not waste CPU computing non-displayed 2D maps!).
  7. Versioned Intensity Cache & Selective R/B Invalidation:
  8. Replace pass-only cache eviction with an LRU/bounded cross-batch cache (e.g., max 64 entries, evicted on remove_map / clear_workspace) keyed cleanly to prevent MapData reload collisions: 
    cache_key = (
    md.name,
    id(md),
    md.data_version,
    param_name,
    round(float(x_min), 6),
    round(float(x_max), 6),
)
  9. Benefit: When only Primary Map is baseline-subtracted or normalized, or when a 2nd/3rd map is added to the selection, unchanged maps hit _intensity_cache in \(O(1)\) without re-integrating hundreds of thousands of spectra.
  10. When Green is configured in R/B ratio mode, compute/fetch I_red and I_blue using the same versioned cache ("Integrated intensity" for Red [r_min, r_max] and Blue [b_min, b_max]). Changing Red bracket updates Red plus Green when Green is in R/B ratio mode; changing Blue updates Blue plus Green similarly.
  11. Vectorized is_active Consistency:
  12. After vectorized compute_spectral_parameter(x_axis, y_matrix, ...) (or before slicing via boolean row index if < 50% active), apply md.is_active consistently:
    • In 2D maps: set values[~md.is_active] = np.nan so compute_map_grid / imshow masks deselected pixels identically to VMapViewer!
    • In 1D profiles: set values[~md.is_active] = np.nan (Matplotlib breaks lines cleanly over NaN gaps without collapsing X indices).
  13. Typed Multi-Profile Payload (multi_profile_data_ready):
  14. Proposed signals: Introduce a structured multi-profile payload signal (while preserving profile_data_ready for single-profile backward compatibility): 
    # Payload list of dicts/dataclasses per profile:
# {"name": str, "positions": np.ndarray, "values": np.ndarray,
#  "axis_label": str, "is_primary": bool, "out_of_range": bool}
multi_profile_data_ready = Signal(str, list, str, str)
# (color_id, entries, shared_x_label, status_msg)
  15. Also emit proposed map_2d_candidates_changed = Signal(list, str, str) (candidate_names, active_name, status_msg) and live_maps_cleared = Signal() so VLiveMaps keeps its tab-level 2D switcher synced and clears cleanly on empty selection.
  16. Determine shared_x_label: uniform axis ("X" or "Y") if all included profiles share it; "Position along profile" when mixing X/Y or diagonal "Distance".
  17. Adaptive Debounce (_recalculate_batch scheduling):
  18. Measure last_compute_plus_emit_ms. Set QTimer interval during continuous bracket drags to max(60, min(250, int(last_elapsed_ms * 1.1))) (leading-edge immediate feel on mouse release via immediate=True or trailing tick) so slow multi-map workloads coalesce rather than stalling Qt's event loop.
